extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of literary criticism; teachers and readers learning to appraise poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating lyric poems and sonnets, focusing on sound (rhythm, rhyme, assonance), sense (imagery, logic, meaning), form suitability, diction, and the reader's method and biases. Emphasises order of judgement (whole then details) and the effects of different renderings/performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cadence and spirit / immediacy on first reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Even the first reading takes you into its cadence and its spirit; it wears better with each succeeding reading that you really have concentrated on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether a poem's rhythm and tonal quality draw the reader in immediately and improve on repeated readings; note whether initial cadence matches the poem's spirit. Example: poem that 'takes you into its cadence' and 'wears better' on further attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity / taste of life
rubrics_metrics.description: Has a taste of life — life as Shakespeare knew it and Hugo, not as Shelley or Keats... full-blooded and perfectly conversant with life as it is in its sorrows, despairs, and its fulfilled and unfulfilled hopes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the poem convincingly portrays lived experience and emotional truth rather than abstract or superficial sentimentality; look for 'punch', energy and vigour tinged with philosophical tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intimacy of voice / sense of friendship
rubrics_metrics.description: Curious way it suggests immediately great intimacy with the author. FRIENDSHIP. A room at night... you and him alone. One of those rare inexplicable moments which stand out as REAL in a world of phantasms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the poem conveys a direct, intimate address or rapport with the reader (a feeling of shared experience or 'friendship'); note techniques that create this intimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation and precision of language
rubrics_metrics.description: Topping condensation of language. No vapid and ineffectual adjectives. Each word contains multitudes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer economy: consider whether words are chosen for dense, multi-layered meaning rather than padded with weak modifiers; flag 'vapid' adjectives and unnecessary verbosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom and balance of lines / musicality
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom and balance of lines. Like wonderful music.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the lineation for a sense of freedom and internal balance; look for musical qualities in how lines flow and balance against one another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of rhyme (don't overvalue perfect rhyme)
rubrics_metrics.description: An exaggerated respect for rhyming ability is the result... By assuming that the poet intended to rhyme perfectly, we get a clear unambiguous test for his success or failure. The assumption need not be explicit... the temptation to entertain it is comprehensible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid allowing imperfect or partial rhymes to dominate judgement; consider whether imperfect rhyme might be deliberate or subordinate to other poetical aims instead of treating rhyme as sole tangible test of merit. Example criticisms about 'thrush'/'bush' show this bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid superficial detail-first judging
rubrics_metrics.description: All those features which can be judged without going into the poem... are so many invitations to make short work of the task of critical appraisement. Instead of trying the poem on, we content ourselves with a glance at its lapels or its buttons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start from an overall judgement of the whole work before drilling into technical details; reversing the process (judging details first) is rash and usually disastrous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive accuracy and logical sense of imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges of descriptive inaccuracy (e.g. 'How can the sun shine "most shadily"?') and logical inconsistency are common criticisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether images/assertions are coherent and sensibly expressed; ask if phrasing creates unintended absurdities or ambiguities. But also weigh whether apparent oddities are deliberate evocative choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scansion and rhythmical reading matter
rubrics_metrics.description: In reading this, one must not let the rhythm become too square-cut. If one does, the whole thing becomes jerky and amateurish: one accentuates faults of scansion and throws emphasis upon the wrong words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider not just printed feet but how reading/intonation shapes scansion; test alternative readings (e.g. different accentuation) to see which best suits the poem's swing and lightness. Poorly read scansion can misrepresent the poem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assonance and sonic devices as legitimate alternatives to strict metre
rubrics_metrics.description: The passage is obviously intended to possess lyrical simplicity. Assonance, rather than strict metre, is used to heighten effect of simplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise sound devices (assonance, sibilance, vowel patterns) as deliberate methods that may substitute for or complement strict metrical regularity in achieving effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication / experiential success
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication extraordinarily successful. Experience most pleasant and refreshing and consolatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the poem successfully communicates the intended experience, feeling or idea to the reader (pleasure, consolation, refreshment); measure the immediacy and clarity of that communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader's mnemonic associations and biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Reminders of our own poetic efforts... have an inevitable influence on our judgment... All but a very few beginners find rhyming a great strain... A tendency to great severity towards verses in which the poet, if concerned only with making his rhymes perfect, could be charged with partial unsuccess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that readers bring personal and mnemonic biases (e.g. memories of their own early poems) that can make them unfairly harsh; try to separate personal associations from objective appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound–sense correspondence (phonetics matching imagery)
rubrics_metrics.description: The vowels are also well arranged... The sudden transition to the long i sound gives an impression of height in the arch... The whispering air is perfectly expressed by the repeated s's in verse 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether phonetic choices (vowels, consonant clusters, sibilance, echo) enhance and mirror the imagery or mood; cite specific sound–sense correspondences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity and spontaneity vs muddled sentimentality
rubrics_metrics.description: The sincerity and spontaneity of this lyric might be contrasted with the muddled sentimentality of [other poem]. In its own rather tiny way, it is quite exquisite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish genuine spontaneous feeling from clumsy or sentimental writing; sincerity often shows in balanced, proportional expression and subtle rhythmic shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of judgement: whole then details
rubrics_metrics.description: The sovereign formula in all reading is that we must pass to judgment of details from judgment of the whole. It is always rash and usually disastrous to reverse the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First form a sense of the poem as a whole (tone, aim, effect), then examine details (rhyme, metre, grammar) to see how they support or undermine that whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider reader's inhibitions and preconceptions when comprehension fails
rubrics_metrics.description: Failures to grasp the meaning... are not easy to range in order. Distractions, preconceptions, inhibitions of all kinds have their part... The assumption that stupidity is a simple quality is wrong; it may be an effect of complex inhibitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When readers fail to construe meaning, probe for external causes (prejudice, ideological bias, technical misconceptions) rather than assuming the poem is obscure or bad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-content appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: The prejudice against the alleged Shakespearean form, or rather against the couplet as a close, is hardly sufficient... Sonnet form unperceived till second reading... A poem of this kind needs perfection. If not, enumerations cannot but bore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the chosen form (sonnet, hymn-like metre, lyric) matches the subject and tone; some subjects demand formal perfection or a particular formal movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diction and ability to heighten trivial words
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an abundance of monosyllables and of trivial words, whose very triviality becomes evident by the failure to heighten them in the same manner as he has done in the opening four lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the poet heightens commonplace or trivial diction through rhythm, sound, or context; strings of monosyllables may flatten intended loftiness if not skillfully handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional trajectory and unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Somehow the poem does not raise as much emotion as one feels it ought to have raised. I think this is because it seems to progress downwards from greater emotion to less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the poem's emotional arc coheres and builds appropriately for its subject; watch for a decline in intensity where escalation or a controlled release is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of memorisation and repeated readings
rubrics_metrics.description: No thoughts would come to me until I had committed these verses to memory. Then I saw that the words and the subject were simple enough, but underneath lay something which I cannot define.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test whether committing lines to memory or multiple readings reveal latent meaning or musical/subtle effects that single readings miss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance, proportion, and sense of pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: With this fine balance and sense of proportion... a delicate sense of pattern which prescribes the changes in the cadence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for proportionate structuring and recurring patterns (cadence, reiteration) that control changes in tone and support the poem's overall architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise evocative adjective choice for atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: The adjectives are chosen with a full regard for their emotive value — in particular, 'mossy stone' which at once produces the intended atmosphere of quietness and uninterrupted peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the emotive value of modifiers and small lexical choices; specific adjectives can immediately establish atmosphere if they are evocative and well-placed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of hostile stock responses to subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: That a stock response, elicited merely by the religious subject-matter, should be able to make a sonnet sound like a hymn is a fact that surely stretches our notions of the mind's power over matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be conscious of automatic negative/positive reactions evoked by certain topics (religion, patriotism) that may color technical judgements; try to separate topic-based prejudice from formal appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of sound-focused readers vs sense-focused readers
rubrics_metrics.description: I should never bother about the sense; the sound is enough for me. He goes very far, as far perhaps as he can get, by the purely sensuous approach. The relation of the second part to the first can only be given by the sense, and missing the sense he mistakes the feeling of the opening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise that readers emphasize different axes (sound vs sense); good criticism notes when an approach (purely sensuous) misses necessary semantic relations that tie the poem together.
